question: Should starting Video Talk and granting browser camera permission authorize OpenAI Realtime to request one-frame captures for the duration of that visibly active session?
rationale: The implementation has no evident secret or transport flaw, but it creates a new privacy boundary where the provider model—not a separate user click—initiates each capture after session consent; the linked issue is explicitly awaiting security review and no security-owner approval is visible.

options.title: Approve session-scoped capture
options.body: Accept the visible preview plus browser permission as consent for bounded model-triggered frames, after catalog gating and live provider proof are added.

options.title: Require per-capture confirmation
options.body: Add an in-product confirmation before each frame is sent, trading conversational speed for stronger explicit consent.

options.title: Defer Video Talk
options.body: Pause this feature until the camera consent and provider-data policy is documented and approved.

recommendation.title: Approve session-scoped capture
recommendation.body: Accept the visible preview plus browser permission as consent for bounded model-triggered frames, after catalog gating and live provider proof are added.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on the shared Talk discovery path makes this the best available routing candidate, although explicit security ownership remains uncertain.
